<description>
Alternative approach to #36688, citing the relevant parts of its description:

[quoted text omitted]
Fix this by only adding a socket to the `select()` exception set while waiting for a non-blocking `connect()` to complete. Windows needs that to detect a failed connection. Established connections no longer monitor the exception set on any platform. This approach was suggested by theuni in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36716#issuecomment-6931290348 and replaces the earlier version of this PR, which ignored the exception set outside Windows and disconnected on it on Windows.

We could instead have set `SO_OOBINLINE` on our sockets, so `recv()` returns any urgent data sent to us (and likely leads us to disconnect the peer). RFC 6093 doesn't forbid this, but the current approach seems more clear and direct to me.

The PR makes one additional change for clarity: instead of `if (recvSet || errorSet)`, check `errorSet` separately and earlier (emits a different log message). Since `select()` no longer reports errors for established connections, this only applies to `poll()`.

Test coverage is introduced in `p2p_socket_errors.py`.

Finally the same early error check is applied to HTTP, with urgent data coverage in `interface_http.py`.
</description>

[2026-11-18] c:6986474295 comment by Sjors (member) (edited 2026-11-18):
@theuni to put it into my own words, IIUC:

There's two phases to a connection, phase 1 establishes it `ConnectToSocket` and phase 2 maintains it after (in `GenerateWaitSockets`, etc). Your proposal makes it so that in phase 2 nothing watches `errorSet`, while in phase 1 it's now watched on all platforms. A follow-up could narrow phase 1 to just Windows as belt-and-suspenders.

This makes sense, and I adopted it.

On ancient versions of Windows it was unsafe to ignore `errorSet`, and it had to be drained to prevent memory exhaustion. See https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/tcpm/55ecR94wP1NkrL5cuPj0PWtTIXc/

The following checks for this:  https://gist.github.com/Sjors/9582259267a038e06c7f0730356416de

I tested on a physical Windows 11 Home 26H2 machine. Connections reset after 17 urgent bytes. I also tested Windows Server 2022 on a Github CI runner: https://github.com/Sjors/bitcoin/actions/runs/44390882699/job/135107875034

The latter should roughly match Windows 10 in this regard, which is the oldest version we support. So this is no longer a concern in theory, but it doesn't hurt to actually try if you can find such a machine.

BSD is probably also worth testing, cc @vasild.
[2026-11-18] rc:4621817780 inline on src/net.cpp by theuni (member) (edited 2026-11-18):
I experimented with removing `select()` entirely on top of this changeset, and ended up needing a little change here. Rather than `recvSet`, what we really want to test (as your comment states) is `recvReq`, where
```c++
bool recvReq = it->second.requested & Sock::RecvEvent;
```

I don't think it matters here, but in order to support poll in a cross-platform way, the exact condition we want to test is "did we see an error when we didn't request a receive event", which is slightly different than "did we see an error when we didn't SEE a receive event" as we have here.

This matters for platforms (Windows) which raise only `POLLERR | POLLHUP` for disconnections, even when `POLLIN` was requested.

Again.. it shouldn't matter here. Just pointing it out for the future.
[2026-11-18] rc:4622012073 inline on src/net.cpp by theuni (member) (edited 2026-11-18):
According to the `poll` Linux manpage, we may receive a lone `POLLHUP` (without `POLLIN` or `POLLERR`) when the socket has been drained and the next recv would close it. I think if we skip the `|| errorSet` here, we could end up waking for the error (`POLLHUP`) event, and never doing anything with it. Then we're back to the tight loop.

Since `select` is a no-op here now, I don't see the harm in leaving this as `if (recvSet || errorSet)` ?

Here's the output of the Linux manpage example. It's a file descriptor rather than a socket, it's possible that the behavior is different.

```bash
 $ ./poll myfifo
Opened "myfifo" on fd 3
About to poll()
Ready: 1
  fd=3; events: POLLIN POLLHUP
    read 4 bytes: foo

About to poll()
Ready: 1
  fd=3; events: POLLHUP
    closing fd 3
All file descriptors closed; bye
```
[2026-11-18] r:5966316401 review COMMENTED by theuni (member):

See my comment about keeping the `(recvSet || errorSet)` check as-is.

Other than that, looks good to me.
